Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: HealthTrust — interim status and immediate mitigations

Hi Asha / team — quick status update following our triage: 

What we saw: kernel-level KV cache churn and increased prefix cache misses in the 08:30–09:15 window that amplified token-generation latency and triggered transient 5xxs from the runtime.

Actions taken (12:00 PT):
- Re-routed HealthTrust traffic to a dedicated capacity pool to isolate noisy neighbors. (david_kim)
- Applied a temporary model routing rule: traffic for heavy-batch jobs now routes to a smaller quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes (expected p95 improvement). (david_kim)
- Stabilized KV cache eviction thresholds to reduce misses — this lowered token-gen time for observed samples. (sean_gallagher)

Immediate effects:
- Error rate for affected endpoints: from ~12% down to ~1.4% in the first 45m post-mitigation.
- p50/p95 latency improved from 210ms/1.8s to 200ms/350ms respectively on the sample workloads.

Next steps / asks:
- We’re continuing to monitor and will keep you updated every 2 hours until stable.
- Can you provide 2–3 production correlation-ids for the last 30m if you see any residual 5xxs?
- We’d like to propose a 30m exec-level sync at 14:00 PT today to walk through impact and any business remediation (open to a Friday afternoon slot if needed).

Opening a follow-up: RDW incident PD-8821, HubSpot: HT-4319. Post-mitigation stats attached.

Appreciate the patience — we’ll own this until you’re green.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 650 555 0219

Subject: HealthTrust — stabilization summary and next steps (internal)

Team — final internal summary after follow-up with customer and engineering: 

Resolution summary:
- Root cause (provisional): compounding KV cache churn + a scheduled batch traffic pattern that amplified cache misses on the shared pool. This elevated runtime CPU bursts and led to transient 5xxs.
- Mitigation: routing to dedicated pool + fallback to quantized variant + cache threshold tuning resolved immediate customer impact.

Customer impact & remediation:
- Customer reported business impact between 08:48–12:00 PT on 2026-09-18; backlog cleared by 13:15 PT after mitigation.
- We offered a customer-facing incident postmortem and a service credit evaluation; HealthTrust accepted a 5% credit on the billing period as a good-faith gesture pending final RCA. Procurement is copied on prior threads.

Follow-ups & owners (target dates):
- Detailed RCA write-up and timeline: Laura to deliver to customer and internal execs by 2026-09-22. Owner: laura_bennett.
- Permanent mitigation: Engineering to propose a routing/cache configuration change and a test plan by 2026-09-29. Owner: sean_gallagher / david_kim.
- Billing & credits: Finance to confirm credit processing and communicate to HealthTrust by 2026-09-24. Owner: laura_bennett (coordination).
- Customer postmortem (customer-facing): Draft due 2026-09-22, send to Asha for review. Owner: tessa_morgan.

Notes: please keep the customer comms clear and non-technical for exec-level recipients; include a brief timeline, actions taken, and the proposed credit. We should avoid mentioning internal kernel names in the customer-facing doc.

Thanks all — good work on the quick mitigation.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
